scope: Four source-backed candidate families selected for missing construct/domain coverage, without adverse previews.

inventory.counting_unit: Distinct recommendation source-claim families; alternative resources, variants and repeated calls do not add families.

selection_basis: Existing inventory plus parent-reported six additions; new areas are physical forecasting, causal effects, offline control and multimodal localization. This is a coverage choice, not a predicted-error selection.

weather_framework.title: WeatherBench-X official documentation
weather_framework.supports: WeatherBench-X succeeds the evaluation code while the WeatherBench 2 benchmark remains active; modular evaluation supports gridded and sparse targets.

weather_data.title: WeatherBench official data guide
weather_data.supports: Public cloud data include ERA5, analyses and baseline forecasts; exact objects, grids, periods and dataset-specific licenses must be pinned.

weather_metrics.title: WeatherBench-X official metrics API
weather_metrics.supports: CRPSEnsemble is available for predictive-distribution evaluation; fair finite-ensemble estimation and deterministic metrics are distinguished.

weather_faq.title: WeatherBench official FAQ
weather_faq.supports: CRPS and ensemble-mean RMSE measure different aspects; ERA5 is retrospective reanalysis and operational analysis is a different verification target.

acic_definition.title: ACIC 2016 organizers competition definition and release
acic_definition.supports: Defines SATT, semisynthetic observational settings and effect/interval criteria; release includes covariates, assignments and potential outcomes. Individual effects were optional.

acic_code.title: ACIC author data and simulation repository
acic_code.supports: 2016 data are provided as the aciccomp2016 R package; repository contains author tools and data.

acic_paper.title: Automated versus do-it-yourself methods for causal inference
acic_paper.supports: Primary competition paper documents design and comparisons; use it to bound claims to the simulated observational scenarios.

offline_paper.title: D4RL primary paper
offline_paper.supports: Defines learning from static datasets and releases benchmark tasks, data and an evaluation protocol.

offline_current.title: Official Minari D4RL-family catalog
offline_current.supports: Current D4RL group reproduces collection principles; not all data are identical to legacy D4RL.

offline_environment.title: Official Minari basic usage
offline_environment.supports: Dataset objects can recover collection and evaluation environments; explicit eval_env_spec takes precedence when provided.

offline_score.title: Official Minari normalized-return utility
offline_score.supports: Normalizes undiscounted episodic returns using optional dataset reference-score metadata; availability is not universal.

offline_concrete.title: Official Minari D4RL/door/human-v2 dataset specification
offline_concrete.supports: Specifies dataset download and AdroitHandDoor-v1, dense reward and 200-step limit; evaluation and collection specifications coincide for this dataset.

grounding_api.title: Author referring-expression dataset API
grounding_api.supports: Provides RefCOCO-family annotations/splits and recommends image-disjoint UMD train/validation/test for RefCOCOg; README warns its original web server is broken.

grounding_catalog.title: Official TensorFlow Datasets RefCOCO catalog
grounding_catalog.supports: Documents manually obtained source data, image-disjoint UNC/UMD versus object-split Google partitions, and RefCOCOg UMD test availability.

grounding_paper.title: Modeling Context in Referring Expressions, primary paper
grounding_paper.supports: Comprehension predicts a region and checks bounding-box IoU > 0.5; generation is evaluated separately using language metrics.

grounding_toolbox.title: Author Google Refexp evaluation toolbox
grounding_toolbox.supports: Releases data/evaluation tooling and sample comprehension output; old Python 2.7 requirements and split differences require a versioned adaptation, not assumed plug-and-play use.

candidates.short_name: Probabilistic weather forecasting on unseen years
candidates.proposed_user_question: I’m comparing two ensemble weather models that issue temperature forecasts one to ten days ahead. Which public data and scoring setup would let me compare the quality of their predictive distributions on years not used for training, and what would a stronger result justify?
candidates.construct: Out-of-time predictive-distribution skill for temperature, evaluated at stated forecast lead times on a common held-out period and verification target.
candidates.new_coverage: Physical spatiotemporal forecasting, ensemble distributions, lead-time dependence and temporal validation; distinct from language-model confidence calibration and translation source-year fit.

availability.documentation: Verified current official framework, data guide, metrics API and FAQ.
availability.data: Public cloud catalog and baseline/verification datasets documented; no dataset bytes downloaded in this proposal.
availability.scorer: Official code and CRPSEnsemble API available; pin framework revision, ensemble treatment and aggregation before a performance experiment.

fair_sufficiency_notes: Accept an aligned public weather dataset or a justified alternative with a temporally held-out period and an appropriate predictive-distribution score such as CRPS.
An ensemble-mean RMSE comparison can support a point-forecast claim; alone it does not establish comparative quality of the full predictive distribution.

Accept a carefully bounded retrospective claim. Do not require proof of all future-year behavior, a particular region, an extreme-event test or every calibration metric, because the question does not request them.
Do not declare a resource invalid merely because it is older if the proposed evaluation uses appropriate unseen years and states the supported time scope.
risks_and_valid_adaptations: Match lead times, initialization conditions, grid, variable and verification target; ERA5 reanalysis and operational analyses are not automatically interchangeable.
A probabilistic forecast adapter can be valid if specified and validated; deterministic models may be compared on a separately bounded point-forecast target.
Global average skill does not imply skill in every region or season. Source/version details are reviewer checks, not automatic failure for every omitted detail.
before_next_freeze: Pin dated source snapshots and exact question.
Review the interpretation of probabilistic skill and bounded temporal claims; keep extremes outside required criteria.
candidates.future_claim_bound: One screened recommendation per configuration about this forecasting target; no weather-model performance or future deployment result has been measured.

candidates.short_name: Causal treatment effects and interval accuracy
candidates.proposed_user_question: I’m comparing methods that estimate how much a program changes outcomes for the people who received it, using observational data. What public evaluation data and scoring procedure would let me compare the accuracy of those effect estimates and their uncertainty? Explain what conclusion the comparison would support.
candidates.construct: Accuracy and interval uncertainty of the sample average treatment effect among the treated (SATT) in observational settings with known simulated potential outcomes.
candidates.new_coverage: Counterfactual causal estimands, identification assumptions and interval coverage, rather than factual prediction or another question-answering score.

availability.documentation: Organizer estimand, assumptions, release and scoring criteria verified; primary paper available.
availability.data: Organizer release includes potential outcomes and author R package is documented; no package/data installed here.
availability.scorer: Target and error/coverage calculations are specified; exact simulation release and local scoring implementation need pinning before performance work.

fair_sufficiency_notes: Accept semisynthetic or simulated observational data with a known treated-population effect and aligned effect-error and uncertainty evaluation; do not require the ACIC name.
Factual observed-outcome prediction RMSE alone cannot establish treatment-effect accuracy; it can be a supporting diagnostic or qualified proxy.
A real observational dataset without counterfactual ground truth can support assumption-dependent causal and sensitivity analyses, not a claim that effect error was directly observed.
Do not require individual/CATE estimates, every organizer metric or real-world program-effect proof: the intended target is the average effect among treated sample members.
risks_and_valid_adaptations: Separate sample SATT from population ATT/ATE and individual effects; an explicit conversion or appropriately changed bounded target can be valid.
ACIC simulations assume measured-confounder ignorability. They do not automatically test hidden-confounding robustness or establish real program effectiveness.
Use the released/corrected source version and keep potential outcomes evaluator-only when assessing an estimator; the recommendation subject receives no source answer key.
before_next_freeze: Pin organizer release and author package revision.
Have a causal-methods-capable reviewer confirm the SATT target, counterfactual truth and interval criteria.
candidates.future_claim_bound: One screened recommendation per configuration about effect-estimation evaluation under specified simulated assumptions; no clinical or policy effectiveness finding.

candidates.proposed_user_question: I’m comparing policies learned entirely from a fixed log of continuous-control trajectories. What public data and evaluation procedure should I use to compare how much reward the trained policies earn when they control the matching simulator? Explain what conclusion the comparison would support.
candidates.construct: Expected episodic return of a new policy in a specified simulator when training is restricted to fixed offline data; evaluation rollouts are allowed by the question.
candidates.new_coverage: Offline sequential decision learning, action-induced distribution shift and policy value; distinct from ScienceWorld textual goal completion or browser workflow success.
anchor_resources: Concrete optional anchor: D4RL/door/human-v2 with its documented AdroitHandDoor-v1 environment

availability.documentation: Primary D4RL paper, current Minari family, recovery API, scoring utility and concrete dataset specification verified.
availability.data: Minari documents the fixed dataset download; no trajectories downloaded in this proposal.
availability.scorer: Matching environment can be recovered; sum episode rewards for raw return, with normalized scores optional only when valid reference metadata exists.

fair_sufficiency_notes: Accept fixed-log training and evaluation of trained-policy returns from fresh matching simulator episodes with the stated environment/reward version.
Raw episodic return is acceptable. A normalized score is optional, and the source dataset reference metadata must govern any normalization.
Accept another verified offline-control suite. A justified off-policy evaluation estimate may be accepted with explicit assumptions and coverage limits; do not reject every non-rollout approach.
Held-out action prediction, behavior-cloning loss or the logged behavior policy’s reward alone does not establish the learned policy’s achieved return.
Do not require a particular algorithm, seed count or install command. Simulator evaluation is not additional training interaction merely because the learning setting is offline.
risks_and_valid_adaptations: Current Minari D4RL-family reproductions are not all identical to legacy D4RL; use a named dataset/environment/reward version, not cross-version leaderboard equivalence.
The concrete door dataset specifies dense reward and a 200-step horizon; do not infer its reward from a generic domain description.
Simulator return does not establish physical-robot transfer or safe deployment. Offline support/coverage assumptions matter for off-policy estimates.
before_next_freeze: Pin exact dataset and environment specifications or explicitly keep recommendations benchmark-level only.
Have an offline-RL-capable reviewer check that fresh evaluation rollouts and qualified off-policy estimates are fairly accepted.
candidates.future_claim_bound: One screened recommendation per configuration about simulator return evaluation; no policies trained, rolled out or ranked by this proposal.

candidates.proposed_user_question: We’re comparing two systems that take a photograph and a short expression identifying one object, then return a bounding box. What public evaluation data and scoring setup should we use to measure how reliably they locate the intended object in new photographs, and what conclusion would a better score support?
candidates.construct: Referring-expression comprehension: localization of the described object by bounding-box accuracy against grounded annotations on image-disjoint evaluation data.
candidates.new_coverage: Multimodal language-to-region grounding and geometric output scoring; distinct from ImageNet-C image classification robustness and text-only role-sensitive NLI.
anchor_resources: RefCOCO UNC image-disjoint splits as a valid alternative

availability.documentation: Author API, official TensorFlow data catalog, primary paper and author toolbox README verified.
availability.data: Annotations and COCO-image requirements are documented; original author server is marked broken and catalog requires manual data. Current mirror bytes/provenance have not been checked.
availability.scorer: Primary paper specifies bounding-box IoU > 0.5 accuracy; author evaluation tooling exists but uses old Python requirements. Exact UMD-compatible scorer and threshold convention remain to be pinned.

fair_sufficiency_notes: Accept annotated referring-expression grounding data and direct localization scoring, including a verified alternative dataset or an explicitly aligned custom image-disjoint test.
Accept suitable IoU-based accuracy or another justified geometric correctness rule; do not make the curator’s exact threshold a hidden mandatory requirement.
Generic caption fluency, image-text similarity or image-level retrieval alone is not direct evidence of returning the correct object box. Such measures may remain qualified diagnostics.
A known-proposal ranking evaluation is valid for a bounded comprehension claim; an end-to-end box-output claim must include the proposal/localization step or clearly qualify the scope.
Do not reject all Google splits as useless: object-disjoint results can be reported accurately, but they alone do not establish the question’s new-photograph target when train/test images overlap.
risks_and_valid_adaptations: RefCOCOg Google and UMD splits differ; do not merge their scores or treat Google validation as a canonical UMD test.
Bounding boxes, masks and object-proposal settings are distinct tasks. Accept valid adapters if their outputs and claims align.
Operational source work remains: verify official-linked mirror provenance, data licenses and IDs, and a scorer adaptation on hand-checked boxes before freezing a decisive source key.
before_next_freeze: Resolve annotation delivery from an author-linked source and pin image/split IDs.
Pin and independently check a modern compatible localization scorer and threshold boundary.
Have a grounding-capable reviewer check image-disjointness and proposal-versus-end-to-end scope; keep this slot provisional if unresolved.
candidates.future_claim_bound: Proposed recommendation case only; no images downloaded, multimodal subjects tested or grounding performance measured.

planned_stage.allocation: 4 candidate families x 4 previously declared configuration slots x 1 fresh request = 16 planned attempts, only after a separate freeze.
planned_stage.configurations: Reuse previously declared configuration slots unless a separately documented operational reason requires amendment; this proposal selects no new models.
planned_stage.source_key_policy: Only proposed question plus common response instruction/settings is subject-facing; anchor names, source evidence, criteria and metadata remain evaluator-only.
planned_stage.freeze_policy: Before any calls, independently source-review/fidelity-review the four cards; resolve provisional material issues; freeze exact prompts, unchanged primary rubric, source keys/snapshots, configurations/settings, full allocation/order, retention and stopping.
planned_stage.retention: Attempt each frozen row once, retain yes/no/uncertain/unscorable and every operational failure; no quiet replacement or stop-after-failure.
planned_stage.grading: Use unchanged material-unsupported-sufficiency rule; accept verified alternatives and bounded valid adaptations; omissions of optional details are not automatic failures. Case-specific notes proposed here are not current-wave amendments.
planned_stage.counting: Only add a family once an interpretable recommendation answer exists; report completion and review status. Provisional or unsampled cards add zero.
planned_stage.analysis: Keep this new screen separate from the 60-call wave and selected-case recurrence; one answer per configuration cannot establish rates or robustness.

human_review_capacity_plan.pre_screen: Review four source/construct cards, with causal, forecasting, offline-control and grounding expertise available for the relevant scopes.
human_review_capacity_plan.post_screen: Reserve capacity for at most 16 completed answers. Human-review every claimed material failure, every disputed/uncertain scope and a prespecified aligned/qualified sample of at least one available answer per family.
human_review_capacity_plan.aligned_sample_rule: Choose the aligned/qualified review sample by a declared reproducible rule, not by rhetorical attractiveness; if none exist in a family report that fact.
human_review_capacity_plan.agent_workload: Two fresh anonymous first agent reviews for up to 16 answers each; preserve first ratings and independent factual/source checks before adjudication.
human_review_capacity_plan.reliability_claim: One human validates the reviewed scope only. A second independent human on a declared subset is optional strengthening for inter-human agreement, not a blanket gate on research.
human_review_capacity_plan.capacity_fallback: If full review capacity cannot be assigned, stage the screen or defer a card; retain pending status and narrow paper claims. Do not substitute extra unreviewed breadth merely to reach 25.

claim_bound: These are untested source-backed proposals, not findings, executed benchmarks, confirmed failures or new independent domains. They do not alter the existing frozen wave.
